description: The figure presents three bar charts—(a) WikiText, (b) PTB, and (c) C4—comparing the perplexity of LLaMA1-7B under two quantization strategies: “Uniform” (blue bars) and “Ours” (orange bars), across four quantization bit levels: 3, 4, 8, and 16 bits. In all three subplots, the x-axis represents “Quantization Bits” with categories ordered as 3, 4, 8, 16, while the y-axis measures “Perplexity” on a linear scale ranging from 0 to 30 in (a) and (c), and from 0 to 400 in (b). In (a) WikiText, Uniform achieves perplexities of ~30, ~27, ~27, and ~27, while Ours achieves ~22, ~19, ~18, and ~18, showing consistent improvement. In (b) PTB, Uniform scores ~410, ~320, ~300, and ~300, whereas Ours scores ~250, ~180, ~185, and ~180, again demonstrating lower perplexity across all bit levels. In (c) C4, Uniform scores ~29, ~25, ~24.5, and ~24.5, while Ours scores ~21, ~18, ~17.5, and ~17.5, maintaining a clear advantage. Across all datasets, the “Ours” method consistently yields lower perplexity than “Uniform” quantization at every bit level, with the largest relative gains observed at lower bit counts (especially 3 and 4 bits). The bars are grouped by quantization bit, with Uniform always positioned to the left of Ours within each group, and no bars are shaded or annotated beyond their color-coded legend.
